name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph. Defined by Delaware Code Title 21 §101(18) and regulated by §4198P; the Truth in E-Bike Marketing Act (House Substitute 1 for HB 439, signed September 24, 2026) tightened the moped rules around it.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 and Class 3 assist only while the rider pedals, cutting out at 20 and 28 mph; Class 2 may be propelled by the motor alone, to 20 mph
The motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label, in Arial at least 9-point, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers of any age must wear an approved bicycle helmet, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer
As on any bicycle, riders and passengers under 18 must wear an approved helmet
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, shoulders, bike lanes, bikeways and bicycle or multi-use paths
Never ridden on a sidewalk under motor power, even where bicycles are allowed there

After notice and a public hearing, the local authority or state agency over a bicycle or multi-use path may ban it there for safety or legal reasons, and may ban it from natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle: no driver's license, registration, title, plate or insurance

A two-wheeler with an electric motor under 2,000 watts that can propel it past 20 mph on its own, or assist past 28 mph, is a moped, which needs a driver's license and is barred from bike lanes, sidewalks and paths closed to motor vehicles; other electric two-wheelers that aren't e-bikes are generally motorcycles
Sellers may not market or label an electric moped or motorcycle as an e-bike, and must disclose in writing its legal class, power, top speed and registration, license and insurance needs
